texts: An adult with repaired tetralogy of Fallot, lost to follow-up, now has ventricular arrhythmia, residual pulmonary stenosis and severe pulmonary regurgitation, and his operative notes are missing.
He should be referred to a centre with adult congenital heart expertise.

There he needs a full assessment, cardiac MRI and an arrhythmia study, and a planned pulmonary valve replacement, often with arrhythmia surgery, by a team that knows these hearts and their reoperations.
Guidelines advise that adults with complex repaired congenital disease be cared for in, or with, a specialist congenital centre.
An MRI or an electrophysiology consult alone does not provide this care, and a mechanical pulmonary valve is a poor choice in this position.
In the picture, Nami steers the boat and the old four-log raft away from the village clinic towards the lighthouse full of experts.
Memory hook: an old four-log raft goes back to the lighthouse of its makers.
